architecture.mechanism: Resonance absorption between photon energy and the potential barrier of a nanometer-scale dopant-rich region, enabling light absorption without passing loss or thermal loss.
architecture.intervention: Fabricate nanometer-scale n-type dopant-rich regions within the p-type silicon crystal of the solar cell to create potential barriers tuned to resonate with visible light photon energies, and implement the proposed voltage-decline control methods to maintain high output voltage.
architecture.expected_effect: Elimination of passing loss and thermal loss for visible light frequencies, yielding a theoretical power conversion efficiency exceeding 70%.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure the external quantum efficiency and current-voltage characteristics of the fabricated Region solar cell under standard AM1.5G illumination; if the measured power conversion efficiency does not significantly exceed the conventional Shockley-Queisser limit and no resonance absorption peak is observed in the spectral response corresponding to the engineered potential barrier, the mechanism fails.
